# Recorded vendor PHY bounds

`<libphy-sha256>/wifi-cold.json` is generated by the comparison tool from
complete primary Wi-Fi cold vendor captures. It contains measured facts,
not raw calibration objects, console logs or vendor code. Board sections use
stand labels such as `s31-a` and `s31-b`; the label-to-MAC binding stays in the
private stand file.

The identity is only the SHA-256 of the `libphy` artifact in
`chips/esp32s31/vendor/artifacts.toml`. The tool selects that hash's directory.
The recorded reference for
`116c7c3a55e2ddfd7937edad2667b5d64717f1967519a0201ca6354246f0b1a2`
applies with any ESP-IDF revision that pins the same libphy. A different
libphy without a recorded reference yields INCOMPLETE with the explicit
reason `no PHY baseline for libphy <sha256>`. An explicitly supplied
reference must have the selected libphy identity too.

```console
cargo vendor-check phy-baseline generate --source s31-a=/path/to/run-a --source s31-b=/path/to/run-b --source s31-b=/path/to/additional-run-b
cargo vendor-check phy-baseline generate --reference /path/to/reference.json --source s31-a=/path/to/run-a --source s31-b=/path/to/run-b --source s31-b=/path/to/additional-run-b
cargo hil run phy-recorded-calibration-cold --chip esp32s31 --board s31-b
cargo vendor-check phy-baseline check --board s31-b --run /path/to/production-run
```

Generation verifies run attachment hashes, board labels, the vendor application
hash, completed primary series and complete readable/unreadable coverage.
Discovery supplies readability only. Failed production comparison does not
invalidate complete vendor measurements. Each board needs at least ten
primary vendor boots; larger complete series are retained, with their actual
sample counts and run IDs. The silicon revision is recorded explicitly
(`generate --revision 0` for the measured rev0 boards).

`generate --reference` rebuilds that reference's exact source series from
authenticated archived primary captures, using current register names, masks
and reviewed metadata. It requires the same libphy, boards, source identities,
sample counts, channel and calibration-object size. No new capture is needed.
Every active word must be present. A captured MMIO word no longer selected by
the current model is removed from the active table and retained in
`provenance.retired-mmio` with its original metadata and measured bounds.
`provenance.retired-series` retains its unmasked value or explicit unreadability
for every original boot, tied to the board and source run/repetition. The
committed reference retains nine such MMIO words. Unknown addresses, missing
active or retired coverage, changed sources and lost retired observations are
refused. Repeated regeneration preserves those original observations.

Schema 2 stores entry identities in sorted maps. Each field, MMIO word or analog
byte records its width/count, address where applicable, signedness, mask and
reviewed exclusion. A scalar shared by both boards is stored only if every
recorded boot of every board agrees. Other entries retain each board's own
min/max arrays and margin, or explicit unreadability. A field margin is its
widest element range; a register margin is its own range width. The same
comparison functions apply those bounds to production. No board envelopes are
merged. CCA counter result words retain their measured bounds and a reviewed
value exclusion: every production capture must still read them. The CCA
window/control word remains subject to the vendor-spread value comparison.

Review keys name current model identities. Loading reviews rejects every
unknown key, including reviews outside the selected lifecycle or PHY image.
A register rename requires remapping its review by address. An obsolete key
is rejected instead of silently restoring vendor-spread comparison.

`PMU.HP_ACTIVE_HP_CK_POWER` retains the current model's readable mask
`0x7ff8000f`: opaque bits 3:0 and the header-defined power/isolation/retention
fields at bits 19:30 in `registers/types/pmu.toml`. The archived primary words
produce the shared masked value `0x19c00000`; restricting those same words to
the former `0x0040000f` projection yields `0x00400000`. The additional set
lanes are CPLL/BBPLL power and their I2C power controls. These are clock policy,
so the reviewed whole-word value exclusion applies while every readable sample
is still required. The whole-word read does not expand a writer's authority:
the mixed-owner partition policy retains the word's ownership, and
`HW31_S31_CK_POWER_READBACK_20261027` establishes preservation outside only
`0x0040000f`, with low4 reading zero after a requested15. It does not establish
the physical function of low4 or a wider write mask.

The document's `signature` contains only `libphy-sha256`. Its `provenance`
retains the capture's IDF revision and vendor application SHA-256, plus the
scenario, register model, relation, reviews and capture/comparison recipe
digests of the original capture interpretation. The active table embeds its
current metadata explicitly. ROM and `esp_phy` pins are historical capture
inputs recorded through the recipe's artifact-manifest digest and the source
repository commits. None of these provenance values participates in baseline
identity or is compared against current pins or recipes. Board provenance
retains silicon revision, UTC date, actual N, source run/repetition, repository
commit/dirty flag and observation digest. Generation applies the current
reviewed interpretation to the retained primary capture data. Full original
captures remain in the local run store and are not committed.

The recorded scenario builds/flashes only the diagnostic image, resets it
for each production capture and uses the reference's channel/readability.
It never builds, flashes or discovers readability on the vendor image.
Unknown board, different silicon revision or libphy, incompatible field/register
metadata, missing readable values or incomplete calibration yields INCOMPLETE. DIFF and INCOMPLETE both fail;
their evidence is retained. A recorded comparison is a state comparison, not
an RF-quality or timing qualification.
Archived production captures may contain the same retired MMIO words; they
remain in their authenticated run attachments and do not participate in active
comparison. Other unexpected addresses or missing active words remain
INCOMPLETE. New captures need only the active reference's readability image.

An IDF, application, ROM, `esp_phy` or recipe change preserves the baseline
when libphy is unchanged; complete production captures yield MATCH or DIFF
under the usual comparison rules. A new board has no reference until measured
and does not inherit another board's ranges. Validation still checks document
schema, complete board/field/register coverage, current field metadata and
bounds. Restart and IEEE 802.15.4 points have no recorded sections here.
Generated JSON is replaced only through the generator, never hand-edited.
